sources: Maestro's first drafts, from the theory core's notes (PLAN.md tasks 2.2 to 2.5)
Drums: the Groove MIDI Dataset's counts (Google LLC, CC BY 4.0), maestro/data/grooves.json (task 3.3)

Trap's entry (task 3.4a, DadCraft's choices Oct 24): ideas in our own words from Wikipedia's "Trap music", "Drill music" and "Roland TR-808" (CC BY-SA 4.0), Ben Duinker's "Good Things Come in Threes: Triplet Flow in Recent Hip-Hop Music" (Popular Music 38/3, 2019) and producers' guides (ideas only); docs/data.md, "Trap, a closer look"

rhythm.why: 16ths with triplet and 32nd turns; sparse kicks.

feel.why: Half-time: hats ride 16ths under a half-time kick and snare.

vocabulary.why: Dark minor: harmonic minor's V, the bII.

leading.why: Dark, wide, sparse pads; little fuss.

progressions.why: Harmony barely moves: one or two chords, a chord every one or two bars; the 808 carries it. A section keeps its loop, and a phrase mostly just goes round rather than closing on V to i.

one chord.why: a single dark chord: the 808 and the melody do the moving

i to VI.why: home and the chord a semitone over its fifth, two bars each: trap's commonest pair

phrygian pair.why: home and the bII a semitone above: phrygian's darkest colour

minor plagal.why: home and its subdominant, a bar each

harmonic minor.why: home and harmonic minor's major V, its leading tone a semitone under home

bright pair.why: for a bright key (melodic trap): home and its relative minor, two bars each

variants.why: Rounds come back as they were: no swapped chords (a Bdim for the bVI isn't trap).

members.why: Dark strings, an 808, a bell lead (DadCraft, Oct 24: the bell and the strings).

pad.why: slow strings (GM's String Ensemble 2), two voices, holding each chord (DadCraft, Oct 24: less busy)

bass.why: The 808: no pattern of its own, a note on every kick held to the next, mostly roots, some fifths and octave jumps; now and then a slide into the next note (DadCraft, Oct 24: about 1 in 6). A synth bass stands in for the 808.

melody.why: a bell (GM's glockenspiel): a one- or two-bar riff going round the section, its beat notes fitted to each chord, a beat of it often in triplets over the straight grid (triplet flow); not shaped over the phrase (DadCraft, Oct 24: it felt stuck, not trap)

loop.why: Trap's lead is a short riff on repeat, with room around it (DadCraft, Oct 24: the bells too busy); it changes between sections, not inside them. It plays every other round, resting between (DadCraft, Oct 24: still too busy).

drums.why: Programmed, as trap is (DadCraft, Oct 24: GMD's human hip hop wasn't trap): written kick patterns the 808 follows, written hat patterns with their rolls, the clap fixed on 3, machine-steady; the kick and clap drop out before a new section, and the play opens on the hats.

patterns.why: Kicks as each bar's 16ths (the clap is on 8); hats an 8th at a time: - none, x an 8th, xx two 16ths, o an open hat, 3 16th triplets, 4 32nds, 6 32nd triplets (a run of 3, 4 and 6 is a roll, louder as it goes). Fills (DadCraft's picks from the auditions, Oct 24): a snare roll into a new section, the falling cascade (16ths over the last two beats, each hit short, stepping down) at the end of an 8-bar run, a reversed cymbal and a crash into each section, a riser before some; the clap on 3 layered over a snare. The cascade off for now (DadCraft, Oct 24: "it's not hitting right"), until he brings a reference.

home.why: the one, the a of 3; then a pickup after the one

bounce.why: the and of 2 before the clap; a late kick into the next round

late.why: the second bar skips its one: a hiccup

double.why: a doubled one, then the a of 3

bars: x x x x x x x x
x x x x x x 3 3
eighths.why: plain 8ths, a triplet roll at the end

bars: xx xx xx xx xx xx xx xx
xx xx xx xx xx xx xx 4

roll on 2.why: a triplet turn before the clap, every bar; 32nds at the end

skippy.why: gaps and turns, an open hat before the end

gallop.why: triplets on every off 8th; a fast roll at the end

bars: xx xx o xx xx xx o xx
open lift.why: open hats on the and of 2 and 4, a long roll
